Phase 3 · Assessment reference

Assessment & Submission

The final committee decision is evaluated as both an auditable technical package and a persuasive oral defense.

Canvas is the submission authority

Canvas remains the authority for due dates, submission mechanics, and the project's course-grade weight. The criteria below preserve the existing written/oral assessment emphasis while aligning it to Phase 3.

Written package · 50% of Phase 3 assessment

Technical evidence

CriterionWeightCommittee-ready standard
Technical accuracy25%Calculations, formulas, sources, and portfolio metrics are correct, traceable, and interpreted.
Evidence bridge25%The market view visibly drives CME assumptions, portfolio weights, securities, and client recommendations.
Stress test & mandate compliance25%Each portfolio is tested against its tripwire; breaches trigger documented corrective action.
Visualization & documentation15%Exhibits communicate the decision clearly and include complete sources and the AI audit.
Client and regulatory constraints10%RRTTLLU constraints change the actual portfolio rather than appearing as generic narrative.

Oral defense · 50% of Phase 3 assessment

Investment-committee pitch

CriterionWeightCommittee-ready standard
Narrative flow & clarity30%The committee tells one coherent story from market view to client action.
Defense of strategy30%Members defend the base case, bear case, trade-offs, and quantitative evidence under questioning.
Professional presence20%The team speaks as advisors to the committee with confident, concise, client-aware language.
Committee cohesion10%All four members contribute, transition cleanly, and can answer beyond their lead workstream.
Visual-aid efficacy10%Slides make the recommendation and key evidence visible at a glance rather than serving as a script.

Final readiness check

Before the committee meeting

  • Executive recommendation and decision memo
  • Technical exhibit book linking macro, mandate, allocation, securities, and risk
  • Client-specific recommendation for all three assigned clients
  • Final decision record with vote, reservations, and implementation actions
  • Visual oral presentation with balanced speaking time
  • Cross-functional Q&A preparation

Q&A standard

Every member must be able to defend the market view, mandate, allocation, security choices, stress test, and trade-offs. The panel may direct a question to a member who did not lead that workstream.
